title: Common-Gate Frequency Response
intro: A CG stage has no capacitor between input and output (with $r_o$ neglected), so there is no Miller multiplication and each node gives a clean pole. Its weak points are a low input impedance, a low input DC level, and sensitivity to resistance in series with the gate.

blocks.alt: Common-gate stage: Vin drives the source node X through RS; capacitor CS from X to ground. The gate is at a bias Vb. The drain connects to VDD through RD, with capacitor CD from the drain output to ground.
blocks.caption: CG stage: $C_S = C_{GS} + C_{SB}$ at the input, $C_D = C_{GD} + C_{DB}$ at the output.

blocks.text: The input node sees $R_S$ in parallel with $1/(g_m + g_{mb})$; the output node sees $R_D$:
Because the input resistance is low, the input pole is usually very high. The stage is used where a low input impedance is wanted and, above all, as the upper device of a cascode.
With finite $r_o$ the input impedance depends on the load $Z_L = R_D \parallel (1/C_D s)$, so the nodes interact:
For a current-source load with capacitance $C_L$ and input capacitance $C_{in}$, the exact result is second order:

blocks.tex: \frac{V_{out}}{V_{in}} = \frac{1 + g_m r_o}{r_o C_L C_{in} R_S s^2 + \left[r_o C_L + C_{in}R_S + (1 + g_m r_o)C_L R_S\right]s + 1}

blocks.text: (replace $g_m$ by $g_m + g_{mb}$ to include body effect). Here $Z_{in} = 1/(g_m + g_{mb}) + 1/[C_L s\,(g_m + g_{mb})r_o]$: at high frequency $C_L$ shorts the output, the gain collapses, and $Z_{in}$ falls to $1/(g_m + g_{mb})$, giving an input pole of $1/[C_{in}(R_S \parallel \frac{1}{g_m + g_{mb}})]$.
Resistance in series with the gate
The gate bias network has some resistance $R_G$. Keeping only $C_{GS}$ (and $\lambda = \gamma = 0$), KVL around the input loop gives

blocks.tex: \frac{V_{out}}{V_{in}} = \frac{g_m R_D}{(R_G + R_S)C_{GS}s + 1 + g_m R_S}, \qquad \omega_p = \frac{1 + g_m R_S}{(R_G + R_S)C_{GS}}

blocks.text: $R_G$ adds directly to $R_S$ and lowers the pole. With $C_{GD}$ instead, the resistance it sees grows to $R_D + (1 + \frac{g_m R_D}{1 + g_m R_S})R_G$ (see the time-constant page). Keep the gate of a CG stage firmly bypassed. With a large source impedance the output impedance of a CG stage also falls at high frequency, which shows up in cascodes.

blocks.title: Poles of a CG stage
blocks.text: A CG stage has $g_m + g_{mb} = 5\text{ mS}$, $R_S = 1\text{ k}\Omega$, $C_S = 150\text{ fF}$, $R_D = 2\text{ k}\Omega$, $C_D = 100\text{ fF}$, $\lambda = 0$. Find the gain and both poles.
blocks.answer: Gain 1.67; poles at 6.4 GHz and 0.8 GHz.

blocks.title: Cost of an unbypassed gate
blocks.text: A CG stage has $g_m = 5\text{ mS}$, $R_S = 1\text{ k}\Omega$, $C_{GS} = 100\text{ fF}$. Find the input pole with $R_G = 0$ and with $R_G = 2\text{ k}\Omega$ (only $C_{GS}$ considered).
blocks.answer: 9.5 GHz falls to 3.2 GHz: a factor of 3.
